instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Back Me Up
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the house meeting, support my reading of the bin rota. Alex swapped weeks with me; swaps move duties, not just names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you only swapped the vacuuming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must distinguish an agreement from your recollection of it. Tell them we need one consistent rule for swaps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll support a rule. I won't say Alex agreed to the bins.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then support the rule. Say 'a week includes all the duties,' please. All, not whichever one Alex remembers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Back me up when I explain that I cover mornings. The manager keeps confusing cover with permanent availability.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't at the meeting where you agreed your hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not asking you to quote minutes. Confirm that mornings are a sensible use of my skills.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't tell him you had an agreement if I didn't hear it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then don't. When I say 'morning cover,' nod at that phrase. Please leave the history to me; you can endorse the scheduling.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've tightened the tap joint. Open it slowly before I start the washing-up; a full blast tells us very little.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It soaked me last time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the apron on and turn it halfway. I'll observe the joint from here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You turn it. I'll observe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The observer needs to know where the repair is. Apron first, please, then your hand on the tap. We are testing one change at a time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste this coffee substitute before I fill my cup. A small sip, please; we're assessing flavour, not thirst.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have proper coffee. Why should I spoil breakfast?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A sample is not a serving. One spoonful, then water to clear your palate; I'll make proper coffee if it fails.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You take the spoonful. Your cup's empty too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need an unprompted reaction. If I taste first, I'll influence yours. One spoonful, please, before you add any sugar.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you call it a quick shop, count the carrying: twelve bags up six flights. Purchase time is not delivery time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Sit down and I'll put everything away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Frozen food first, please. I went back for the peas; that was a second trip up those stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you get two rests. I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say 'two trips' when you tell the others. Two rests sounds like poor stamina. Please report the work, not just the recovery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I spent Saturday on your fence. Please don't describe that as putting up three panels; preparation is part of the job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But there are only three panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three panels after removing the rotten posts and making two supply runs. Count the whole operation, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll recommend you to next door. They've got six panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell them three took a full day before you mention six. I would like my Saturday acknowledged, not multiplied.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift. Choose which job I'm doing; sauce doesn't pause politely when I leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you put dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A timer measures time. It does not stir. Gravy or station, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Gravy. I'll get a taxi. Just bring my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase or smooth gravy. I need one instruction that doesn't require me to leave the other one unattended.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The depot shuts at six and your mother's waiting at the station. Those are two stops, not one errand. Which comes first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The parcel is her birthday present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That explains its purpose, not its priority. Mother or parcel, please; I need a route before I start driving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Parcel. I'll ring Mum and explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me now. Shall I answer before leaving, or let it ring while I drive to the depot? Please don't schedule both for the same minute.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Move It for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move your haircut and put our lunch in that slot. A diary records priorities, not just appointments.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've had that booking for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you've had this friend since school. We schedule by importance, not by the date somebody wrote an entry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They charge twenty pounds to change it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pay the change fee. Replace the haircut with my name, please; don't squeeze me into the margin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the quiz for my exhibition opening. Name a deputy before you go; that's how a captain hands over properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll think I've abandoned them for my sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delegation isn't abandonment. Give the deputy the answer sheet and tell the team where you're going.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave after round one and say I've got a headache.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No: 'My sister's opening.' Give them the correct reason when you hand over. Don't make coming to me sound like sick leave.
